title: Ralph Task Executor Schema
description: JSON schema for tasks.json used by Ralph - a Claude Code task orchestrator with parallel execution support

projectName.description: Name of the project these tasks belong to

workflow.description: Workflow-level settings that control behavior after task execution

onTaskComplete.description: Actions to perform when a task completes

commitChanges.description: If true, automatically run git add -A && git commit after each task completes. Defaults to true when workflow is omitted.

commitMessageTemplate.description: Template for git commit messages. Supports {taskId} and {taskTitle} placeholders

parallel.description: Settings for parallel task execution using git worktrees

enabled.description: Enable parallel execution of independent tasks via git worktrees

maxConcurrent.description: Maximum number of tasks to run concurrently in separate worktrees

conflictStrategy.description: Single conflict strategy (legacy). Used only when conflictStrategies is not set. 'claude' asks Claude to resolve, 'abort' falls back to sequential, 'auto-theirs'/'auto-ours' uses git merge strategies.

conflictStrategies.description: Ordered fallback chain for merge conflicts. The first entry decides the initial merge -X flag (for auto-*); the remaining entries are tried in order if the merge or previous step fails. Example: ['auto-theirs', 'claude'] auto-merges trivial conflicts and asks Claude only for the cases -X theirs cannot resolve (add/add, rename/delete). Takes precedence over conflictStrategy when present.

sharedWorktreeObjects.description: Use 'git worktree add --shared' to share .git objects across worktrees. Requires git 2.10+. Falls back gracefully if unsupported.

notifications.description: Webhook notifications dispatched once per session at completion. URLs may also come from RALPH_WEBHOOK_URL.

onComplete.description: Webhook URL to POST a JSON payload when a session completes successfully

onFailure.description: Webhook URL to POST a JSON payload when a session fails. Falls back to onComplete if omitted.

format.description: Webhook payload format. Omit/null → auto-detect by hostname (hooks.slack.com → slack, discord(app)?.com → discord, else → generic). Slack uses {text, blocks}; Discord uses {content, embeds}; generic uses Ralph's structured JSON.

logRetentionDays.description: Auto-delete logs in .ralph-logs older than N days at the start of each --run session. Overridden by RALPH_LOG_RETENTION_DAYS env.

budgetUsd.description: Cumulative cost ceiling (USD). New tasks are blocked once total >= this. Priority: CLI --budget-usd > env RALPH_BUDGET_USD > this > unlimited.

taskTimeoutSec.description: Per-attempt Claude invocation timeout (seconds). Process tree is killed on timeout. Priority: CLI --task-timeout > env RALPH_TASK_TIMEOUT_SEC > this > unlimited.

maxRetries.description: Max retry attempts per Claude call. Priority: env MAX_RETRIES > this > 2.

retryDelay.description: Delay (seconds) between retries. Priority: env RETRY_DELAY > this > 5.

verifyRetries.description: Max self-fix retries when verification.command exits non-zero. 0 disables retry. Higher values cost more tokens but increase recovery odds for flaky/test failures.

smokeTest.description: Single command run on the base branch after each parallel batch's merges complete. Catches semantic conflicts that survived auto/claude conflict resolution. Failure stops the run with non-zero exit. If omitted, Ralph auto-infers a smoke test from repo-root markers (.csproj/.sln → dotnet build, package.json → npm test, Cargo.toml → cargo build, go.mod → go build). Disable entirely with --no-smoke-test (or RALPH_NO_SMOKE_TEST=true). Explicit values here always take precedence over auto-inference.

command.description: Shell command to run on base branch after merges

categories.description: Custom task category list used by PlanGenerator. Defaults to ['plan','implementation','testing','commit']. Override to support different stage patterns (e.g. ['design','impl','docs']).

apiSpecs.description: Optional API specification references that tasks may consult

samplePages.description: Optional sample page definitions that tasks may reference

tasks.description: Ordered list of tasks to execute. Tasks are processed in array order; the first task with done=false is picked next.

id.description: Unique task identifier. Used in --task <id> flag and commit messages.

title.description: Short human-readable title for the task

description.description: Detailed description of what the task accomplishes

phase.description: Project phase this task belongs to (e.g., phase1, phase2)

category.description: Category or domain of the task

done.description: Whether this task has been completed. Set to true by Ralph upon completion.

prompt.description: The prompt text sent to Claude Code for execution. If omitted or empty, Claude Code will not be invoked for this task.

outputFiles.description: List of file paths expected to be created or modified by this task

modifiedFiles.description: List of file paths this task will modify. Used to detect potential merge conflicts for parallel execution.

dependsOn.description: List of task IDs that must be completed before this task can run. Used for dependency resolution and parallel execution planning.

subtasks.description: Optional ordered list of subtasks within this task

verification.description: External verification command run AFTER Claude finishes the task. Exit code 0 = pass; non-zero = task failed (with stdout/stderr fed back to Claude for one self-fix retry). Use this on testing/build tasks so success is determined by tools (pytest, go test, tsc --noEmit, dotnet test, eslint, ...) rather than Claude's self-report.

command.description: Shell command to execute in the task working directory (worktree for parallel mode, repo root for sequential). Run via /bin/sh -c on POSIX, cmd /c on Windows.

timeoutSec.description: Kill the verification process if it exceeds this many seconds. Treated as failure with TIMEOUT marker.

id.description: Unique subtask identifier within the parent task

title.description: Short human-readable title for the subtask

done.description: Whether this subtask has been completed

prompt.description: Optional prompt for this specific subtask
